    Concrete reduced-word Hilbert space with Naimark defect fibers (free-product Hilbert crux, node 3) #

    Node 1 (ReducedWord) built the ABSTRACT reduced-word l2 Hilbert sum Khat K0 H over an arbitrary defect family K0 : X → Type; node 2 (NaimarkDefect) built the CONCRETE per-factor defect space finiteDefectSpace (E x) = (range V_{E x})ᗮ for each factor POVM E x. This node is the INSTANTIATION that joins them: a family of factor POVMs E : X → Fin m → End H (the card X measurements, each with m outcomes) fixes the concrete defect family concreteDefect E x := finiteDefectSpace (E x), and KhatConcrete E := Khat (concreteDefect E) H is the concrete reduced-word Hilbert space. The common-H vacuum concreteVacuum E is node 1's empty-word inclusion, specialized here.

    No hypotheses are needed: the defect space and the l2 vacuum are defined for an arbitrary E (POVM positivity/normalization enter only later).

    Scope caveat (inherited from ReducedWord). KhatConcrete E uses the ℂ-tensor fibers, so it is the scalar-vacuum (H = ℂ) free-product space. It is NOT the operator-valued Boca space (which needs H-relative Connes-fusion tensors); for dim H > 1 the ℂ-tensor over-counts (single-x sector d + d² vs the required 2d), so KhatConcrete E does NOT carry the factor PVM Q x i for general H. These are true kernel-trio facts about the scalar-vacuum space; the concrete NaimarkDefect inputs (K_x ≅ H ⊕ K°_x) are reusable in the correct construction. The closed permanence proof uses the separate direct-sum dilation in BocaDilation*, not this over-counting scalar-tensor route.
